title: Lake Biofilms Sampling
author: Frederic Rimet
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfk4jkyw

steps.title: Select Sampling Season and Sites
steps.instruction: Choose the sampling period and locations based on environmental conditions and lake geography.

substeps.instruction: Perform sampling during summer.
Select sites free of submerged and emergent macrophytes to avoid shadowing effects.
Ensure no strong wind-induced waves or storms have scoured biofilms in the previous 2-3 weeks.
Verify that water levels have been stabilized for at least the last 3 weeks.

Select at least 10 stations per lake, typically every 0.5 to 1.5 km along the shoreline, or densify sampling in heterogeneous areas (e.g., river mouths, wastewater treatment plants, harbors, or quarries).

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Prevent Contamination
steps.instruction: Apply cleaning precautions to avoid sample contamination.

substeps.instruction: Use new nylon brushes (e.g., toothbrushes).
Clean the tray at the lab with 10% H2O2, rinse with DNA-free water, and dry.
Wear gloves throughout the process and change them between different sampling stations.

steps.title: Collect Biofilm Samples
steps.instruction: Collect biological material based on the available substrate at the sampling site.

substeps.instruction: If stones are available: Collect at least 5 stones (total brushed surface ≥ 100 cm²) at 20-50 cm depth from the minimum annual water level within a 100 m² area (at least 2 m wide).
If stones are not available, but artificial/hard substrates (e.g., riprap, concrete) are present: Use a hoe equipped with a net to scrap a minimal surface of 100 cm³ at 20-40 cm depth.

If no stones or hard substrates are available: Squeeze submerged filaments (e.g., Elodea, Potamogeton) or scrap at least 20 cm of macrophyte stem (e.g., Typha) at 20-40 cm depth. Note: Indicate 'macrophyte' on the label; only diatom analyses can be performed.

steps.title: Process Stone Samples in Tray
steps.instruction: Extract the biofilm from collected stones using a cleaning tray.

substeps.instruction: Let the collected stones drain for a few minutes.
Fill the bottom of the tray with 50 ml of DNA-free water.
Brush the stones in the tray, cleaning the top and sides but not the surface that was in contact with the ground.

steps.title: Sub-sample for DNA Analysis
steps.instruction: Prepare samples for DNA extraction from the biofilm/water mixture.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the biofilm/water mixture from the tray into a tube up to 10 ml.
Add approximately 40 ml of absolute ethanol to reach a total volume of 50 ml.
Shake to homogenize and label.
Store at 4°C in the dark for maximum 1 month, or freeze at -20°C or -80°C for maximum 3 months.
Take a second 10 ml sub-sample of the biofilm/water mixture from the tray.
Add a preservative solution: either 70% Ethanol or 2% Formaldehyde.
Store at ~ +4°C in the dark.
Optional: For live inspection (especially soft algae), keep a third sub-sample without fixation and store at ~ +4°C in the dark.

steps.title: Create Blank Samples
steps.instruction: Generate a blank sample for DNA analysis quality control (approximately 1 blank per 10 stations).

substeps.instruction: Fill the bottom of a clean tray with 50 ml of DNA-free water.
Fill a 50 ml sterile Falcon tube up to 10 ml with water from the tray.
Add approximately 40 ml of absolute ethanol to reach a total volume of 50 ml.
Shake to homogenize, label, and store (4°C in dark for 1 month, or -20/-80°C for 3 months).

steps.title: Label and Document Samples
steps.instruction: Ensure all samples and sites are properly recorded.

substeps.instruction: Label samples with: 'Biofilm', 'River Name', 'Station', and 'Date'.
Complete field sheets including Station description (A), Sample description (B), Shore description (C), and Land use description (D).
Provide photographic documentation of the sampling area if possible.
